newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Accord in sight on television directive.
newsitem.headline: Accord in sight on television directive.

text.p: The Council of Ministers and the European Parliament have every chance of agreeing on April 16 on how to revise the 1989 television without frontiers directive, EU officials said on Friday.
The conciliation procedure on how to revise 89/552/EEC will start on that day and could also end then, rather than lasting the six weeks provided for, they said.

The only potential stumbling block is the parliament's demand for an arrangement to ensure that all viewers have the chance to see major sporting events on television free, when exclusive rights are snapped up by pay television channels.

The Council wants three major sports events -- the summer and winter Olympic Games and the Soccer World Cup to be available to all and for other sporting events, decided by member states to be important, to be guaranteed on a mutual recognition principle, while avoiding the system of national lists proposed by the European Commission.
The parliament's second major demand which arose from its second reading is unlikely to raise difficulties.
It called in November for all new television sets to be fitted with so called V-chips to screen out violent programmes from children.
The parliament is expected to agree to a European Commission plan to produce a communication on the isue by the end of the year.
If the two institutions do agree on April 16 the parliament will be able to vote on the revised directive at its May plenary session and the June 30 Culture Council will be able to formalise it.
